html:
The People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan (PDPA) was the Marxist party that ruled Afghanistan from the Saur Revolution of 1978 until 1992. It was founded in Kabul in 1965 by a small circle of teachers, officers and civil servants.

It split almost at once into two wings. Khalq (the Masses), led by Taraki and Amin, drew mostly Pashtun from the villages and army. Parcham (the Banner), led by Babrak Karmal, drew more from Kabul's educated city class. They fought each other even while in power. Amin killed Taraki in 1979, and Soviet troops removed Amin and installed Karmal.

After the Soviets left, Najibullah renamed it the Watan (Homeland) Party in 1990 and spoke of national reconciliation. The government collapsed in April 1992, and the mujahideen took over.
sum: The People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan (PDPA) was the Marxist party that ruled Afghanistan from the Saur Revolution of 1978 until 1992. It was founded in Kabul in 1965 by a small circle of teachers, officers and civil servants.
